tools.name: kanna_info

tools.name: kanna_get_task
tools.description: Fetch one Kanna task's detail: current workflow name (workflowName), stage, activity, workspace branch (branch), pull-request URL (prUrl), worktree path, blockers, latest stage-run result (latestRun), the revision-round budget (revisionRounds, revisionLimit), and its place in the task tree — parentTaskId upward, childTaskIds downward. childTaskIds lists the task's direct children oldest first and includes closed ones, so a fan-out that lost the ids it created (compaction, a resumed session) rediscovers them here rather than re-listing the repo; a finished child is exactly the one an orchestrator must reconcile.

tools.name: kanna_list_task_children
tools.description: List this task's direct children only, including closed children, in chronological order. Each child exposes its workflow identity (workflowName), plus the agent and verdict from its latest recorded stage run; workflowName distinguishes runless specialty-review children from unrelated direct children. Use this durable history to join and reconcile a fan-out after notifications, compaction, or session resume; it is not an arbitrary closed-task listing.

tools.name: kanna_wait_task
tools.description: Block until a Kanna task finishes or closes, polling its detail. A task counts as finished once its latest stage run reaches a terminal status (succeeded or failed) — the recorded verdict, not the agent's live terminal state — so a task whose agent stopped and settled to activity 'idle' resolves exactly like one that settled to 'unread'. Returns the task detail plus waitOutcome 'resolved'; read the verdict from latestRun. If the wait window elapses first it returns the latest detail with waitOutcome 'timeout' instead of failing — that is a normal result, so call it again in a loop to keep waiting.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task id (stable across stages) or one of the task's branch names (task-{id} or task-{id}-{n}).

params.name: timeout_secs
params.description: Seconds to wait before returning the latest detail with waitOutcome 'timeout' (clamped to at most 240, so the call returns inside the 300s tools/call timeout MCP clients enforce).

params.name: poll_secs
params.description: Seconds between polls (minimum 1).

params.name: until
params.description: 'finished' resolves when the task's agent stops or the task closes; 'closed' resolves only when the task closes.

tools.name: kanna_wait_events
tools.description: Watch several Kanna tasks at once: blocks until any of them emits an event, then returns every event since your cursor plus a new cursor. This is the tool for orchestrating child tasks — kanna_wait_task blocks on one id and resolves only on finish, so it cannot watch a fan-out. Scope it by task_ids, by parent_task_id (your own id, to watch everything you fanned out without naming it), or by repo_id. Event types: 'task.created', 'run.started', 'run.finished' (payload.status succeeded/failed/cancelled, payload.result), 'stage.changed', 'task.workflow_changed', 'task.pr_created', 'task.revision_requested' (payload.exhausted true means the task is parked for its human — stop waiting), 'task.closed', 'task.awaiting_input' (the daemon positively identified an interactive prompt and the agent needs an answer, e.g. via kanna_send_task_input), 'task.activity_changed' (the provider-neutral fallback when activity moves from working to idle or unread; payload always includes previousActivity and activity and includes waitingPromptSnippet only when non-empty; this weaker edge does not prove a lasting stop or that the snippet is a question, so confirm it through the debounced kanna_get_task before acting), 'task.merge_signaled' (the task's PR reached the repo's merge agent; payload.source is 'agent' or 'engine'), and 'task.merge_handoff_missing' (the workflow finished a stage that promised the merge handoff with no PR to hand off, so the task was NOT closed — treat it as a failed approval), and 'task.transfer_finalizing' (a cross-machine transfer is shutting the task's agent down so its conversation can be shipped; payload.phase is one of 'wrap-up-sent', 'idle', 'quit-sent', 'exited', 'already-exited', 'degraded'). Prompt text changing while a task remains idle or unread does not produce another event; read waitingPromptSnippet from kanna_get_task when reconciling a stopped task. Call it in a loop, passing back the opaque cursor you were given unchanged: events that fire between two calls are delivered on the next one, each exactly once. Omit the cursor on the first call to receive the retained history. An elapsed window returns waitOutcome 'timeout' with no events — a normal result, not an error. Fixed task/repo scopes use one sequence watermark. parent_task_id binds that same global watermark to the parent id in a constant-size cursor; membership is evaluated at each read checkpoint, so reparenting never rewinds acknowledged events and newly eligible events after the checkpoint are delivered without cursor growth. hasMore true means another batch is already waiting, so call again immediately. In kanna-mcp, task_ids supplied without machine_id may belong to different currently reachable machines: the adapter discovers each owner, waits on all owners concurrently, tags every event with machineId, and returns one aggregate opaque cursor. Pass that cursor back unchanged. A machine_id pins the entire wait to one machine; parent_task_id and repo_id remain machine-scoped and use the local machine unless machine_id is supplied.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Task ids (or branch names) to watch, e.g. the child tasks you created. Required unless parent_task_id or repo_id is given.

params.name: parent_task_id
params.description: Watch every task fanned out under this parent instead of naming ids: pass your own task id and you get your children's events without remembering what you created. Re-resolved on every call, so a child created after you started watching is in scope on the next one. Direct children only, and the parent's own events are excluded — the same set kanna_get_task reports as childTaskIds. Ignored when task_ids is given; takes precedence over repo_id.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Watch every task in this repository instead of naming ids. Ignored when task_ids or parent_task_id is given.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Cursor returned by the previous call. Omit on the first call to receive the retained history for the scope.

params.name: timeout_secs
params.description: Seconds to block before returning waitOutcome 'timeout' with no events (clamped to at most 240, so the call returns inside the 300s tools/call timeout MCP clients enforce).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum events in one response (1-500, default 100). When more are pending the response sets hasMore.

tools.name: kanna_set_task_notify
tools.description: Set or clear the task that is notified when this task finishes: that task's terminal receives 'TASK <id> DONE [success|failure|closed]: <title>' as input. The status is one of exactly three words: success (ended cleanly), failure (its terminating run reported failure, or its agent process died), closed (closed before finishing its workflow — not a failure). Unlike the creation-time notify_task_id this works on an already-running task, so an orchestrator can adopt tasks it did not create. Notification routing is independent of parent_task_id and does not make the task a child. Omit notify_task_id to stop notifying. For watching many tasks at once, prefer kanna_wait_events.

tools.name: kanna_set_task_workflow
tools.description: Change an open task's workflow and pin the new workflow definition. The new workflow must contain a stage with exactly the task's current stage name; incompatible switches are rejected without changing the task. A running stage run and its live session are left untouched: the newly pinned workflow governs the task when that run next transitions. Revision rounds already spent carry over, and changing a workflow does not change the repo's sticky creation-time workflow choice.

tools.name: kanna_list_agents
tools.description: List every resolved named agent definition available to task creation for a repository. Each result includes the invokable name, resolved frontmatter description, definition default provider, model, and effort, and source (built_in, repo_override, or repo_authored). A null defaultProvider means task creation falls back to the configured user default. Repo AGENT.md files win over built-ins by name, and repo EXTEND.md files are already layered into the reported defaults. Definitions declaring `visibility: internal` (stage posts Kanna binds itself, such as commit and approve) are excluded from this listing but still resolve when named explicitly.

tools.name: kanna_create_task
tools.description: Create a new Kanna task: forks a worktree and starts the workflow's first stage agent with the prompt. When called from a Kanna task session, repo_id defaults to the current task's repo. `agent` optionally names any resolved agent definition returned by kanna_list_agents to run the task's first stage with, overriding the workflow stage's own agent binding. Ordinary durable repository work is top-level by default, even when an orchestrator creates it: use notify_task_id to route completion without parent_task_id. Set parent_task_id only for a genuine semantic subtask in a decomposition or fan-out.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Repository id from kanna_list_repos. Optional inside a Kanna task session, where it defaults to the current task's repo.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Task prompt given to the first stage's agent.

params.name: display_name
params.description: Short human-readable task title shown in the sidebar. Omitting it does not derive a title: the task falls back to the prompt text itself, clipped to fit, so tasks whose prompts share an opening line become indistinguishable. Always pass one when creating several tasks from a template.

params.name: workflow_name
params.description: Workflow to run, by review depth: 'no-review', 'single-reviewer', or 'specialized-reviewers'. Defaults to the repo's configured workflow. Internal workflows Kanna binds itself are not choices here — only name one if an agent definition tells you to.

params.name: agent
params.description: Any resolved agent definition name. kanna_list_agents lists the choices — definitions declaring `visibility: internal` are excluded from that listing but still resolve here when an agent definition tells you to name one. It runs the first stage instead of the stage's own agent binding; repo overrides and EXTEND.md layering are honored.

params.name: base_ref
params.description: Git ref to fork the task's branch and worktree from. Defaults to the repo's default branch.

params.name: agent_provider
params.description: Explicit agent provider id: 'claude', 'copilot', 'codex', 'opencode', or 'antigravity'. When omitted, Kanna uses the selected stage or agent definition's provider candidates, then the configured user default.

params.name: agent_type
params.description: 'pty' runs the agent CLI in an interactive terminal session; 'agent' runs it headless via the SDK.

params.name: model
params.description: Model id passed verbatim to the selected agent CLI: Claude uses '--model <id>', Copilot uses '--model=<id>', and Codex/OpenCode use '-m <id>'; Antigravity rejects model overrides. An explicit value overrides agent-definition frontmatter; omit it to use the provider default. Kanna does not maintain a model-id allowlist.

params.name: effort
params.description: Provider-native reasoning effort passed without normalization. Codex uses model_reasoning_effort and validates against the selected model; Claude uses --effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); Copilot uses --effort (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max); OpenCode uses --variant and validates against the selected model; Antigravity uses --effort (low|medium|high). Explicit task effort overrides repo agentProviders effort, then layered agent-definition frontmatter.

params.name: permission_mode
params.description: Permission mode passed to the agent CLI, in camelCase: 'dontAsk', 'acceptEdits', or 'default'.

params.name: parent_task_id
params.description: Existing durable work-item id to nest this task under as a genuine semantic subtask in a decomposition or fan-out. Omit for ordinary top-level work and when the creator merely owns, assigns, or monitors it; completion routing belongs in notify_task_id.

params.name: notify_task_id
params.description: Task id to notify when this task finishes: that task's terminal receives 'TASK <id> DONE [success|failure|closed]: <title>' as input. The status is one of exactly three words: success (ended cleanly), failure (its terminating run reported failure, or its agent process died), closed (closed before finishing its workflow — not a failure). This is independent of parent_task_id: notifying an orchestrator does not make the new task its child.

params.name: allowed_tools
params.description: Allow-listed tool names passed to the agent CLI.

params.name: blocker_task_ids
params.description: Task ids that must finish before this task; it shows as blocked until they do.

tools.name: kanna_signal_agent
tools.description: Find or create a singleton task for an agent in a repo and send it an ordinary policy request. The response's 'created' says which happened: the provider and effort overrides below only apply to a task this call creates, because an already-running singleton keeps the session it was spawned with. Requests may be sent to the merge singleton for its repo-defined policy to assess.

params.name: agent_provider

It overrides the agent definition's own provider candidates and the configured user default, so pass it to run e.g. the merge agent as claude when the default would pick another provider. Ignored when the agent's task is already running.

params.name: effort
params.description: Provider-native reasoning effort for a singleton task this call creates, passed without normalization. Codex uses model_reasoning_effort and validates against the selected model; Claude uses --effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); Copilot uses --effort (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max); OpenCode uses --variant; Antigravity uses --effort (low|medium|high). Ignored when the agent's task is already running.

tools.name: kanna_signal_merge_handoff
tools.description: Send the resolved task, PR, head, base, and summary to the repo's merge singleton as an ordinary policy request. The merge agent applies the repository's checked-in policy; Kanna does not attest approval eligibility or bind the request to saved branch metadata.

tools.name: kanna_send_task_input
tools.description: Send ordinary input text to a Kanna task's live daemon PTY session as one logical message with its own Enter. Delivery is live-session-only and fenced to the PTY process ID observed before acceptance while holding the task's lifecycle lease. If raw desktop or mobile terminal input has opened an unsent draft, the daemon queues the logical message FIFO until that draft crosses its next CR/LF boundary; the queue survives client/server reconnects and daemon handoff, but is never carried into a later run or stage. If no live input-capable agent session exists, or that session is replaced before acceptance, the call fails with reason no_live_agent_session and reports the latest run status and finish time when available; use kanna_resume_task to preserve provider context when possible, or kanna_rerun_stage to start fresh. A delivery_uncertain failure means the daemon may already have accepted the message and it must not be retried blindly. This can steer a merge singleton under its repo-defined policy.

A transition forks a fresh branch and worktree from the committed tip and starts the next stage's agent there; the task id stays the same. Advancing past the final stage closes the task.

tools.name: kanna_resume_task
tools.description: Recover a Kanna task whose latest run is cancelled or failed and whose daemon session is dead. Kanna restarts the same stage in the same worktree and resumes the recorded provider conversation when supported. If provider resume is unsupported or a provider id, transcript, worktree, or other context precondition is unavailable, this is not an endpoint failure: Kanna starts fresh and records the exact reason in latestRun.resumeFallbackReason; latestRun.resumedFromRunId is set only for a real resume. A task-state precondition failure returns an explanatory conflict. An empty 404 means the connected Kanna server is an older server that does not provide this route; inspect kanna_info. When recovery is unavailable or a deliberately fresh conversation is acceptable, fall back to kanna_rerun_stage.

Agent-requested revisions are budgeted per task: the response's revisionBudget reports rounds/limit, and once the budget is spent the request starts nothing and the task parks for its human (revisionBudget.exhausted) — report your findings and stop instead of retrying.
